item.title: Only One Woman Survived The Lane Bryant Massacre
item.description: A gunman entered a Lane Bryant store in Tinley Park, Illinois, and forced six women into the back before opening fire. Five were killed execution-style, while one employee survived by narrowly avoiding a fatal shot and playing dead. More than 18 years later, the killer has never been identified, making it one of America's most haunting unsolved mass murders

item.title: Did Her Own Mother Sell Her For $1,000?
item.description: Six-year-old Joshlin Smith disappeared from her home in South Africa, sparking a nationwide search that ended with a shocking twist. Prosecutors alleged her own mother and two accomplices sold the little girl for about $1,100, and all three were later convicted of kidnapping and human trafficking—yet Joshlin has still never been found.

item.title: Was Cindy James Being Stalked Or Was It All Staged?
item.description: For seven years, Cindy James reported relentless stalking, violent attacks, and terrifying threats that police struggled to explain. When she was found dead under bizarre circumstances, investigators questioned whether she had been the victim of a killer or whether the entire ordeal had been an elaborate deception, leaving one of Canada's most debated true crime mysteries

item.title: They Found Her Car But Not The Truth
item.description: Sixteen-year-old Kiely Rodni disappeared after attending a party in California, sparking a massive search involving hundreds of volunteers and investigators. Days later, her car was discovered submerged in a reservoir, but the circumstances surrounding her final hours continue to raise difficult questions.
